name: Africa Prudential
source: Africa Prudential Plc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023 (audited): statement of profit or loss page 33, earnings per share note 14 page 56; FY2021 from the audited 2021 financial statements filed with NGX; figures in thousands of naira, FY2025/FY2024 as previously recorded | CRON 20260929_195546: operating expenses replaced with the printed total operating expenses from the five year financial summary; the previous row was a different expense line. Verified against printed profit before tax. | CRON 20261005: added Operating Profit (EBIT) from the audited statement of profit or loss, page 36 of the FY2025 annual report, printed as Profit before finance costs and tax, thousands of naira stored as absolute naira. FY2025 4,258,110 and FY2024 2,810,359. Ties: 7,190,107 gross earnings plus 283,776 other income less 213,496 credit loss less 1,157,118 personnel less 1,695,989 other operating less 62,172 depreciation less 86,998 amortisation equals 4,258,110, and the statement prints 4,258,110 as both profit before finance costs and tax and profit before income tax; 4,258,110 less 1,540,938 equals 2,717,172 profit after tax. | CRON 2026-10-07 NGX Q2 2026 filing fill: Statement of profit or loss, six months ended 30 June 2026 column, NGN thousands. Revenue 742,318; Cost of sales 71,573; Gross Profit 670,745; Interest income 3,457,559; Other income 82,694; Net Operating income 4,210,998; Credit loss expense 20,619 plus Personnel 968,451 plus Other operating 753,400 plus Depreciation 33,610 plus Amortisation 27,490 gives total operating expenses 1,803,570; Profit before finance costs and tax 2,407,428; Finance costs nil; Profit before income tax 2,407,428; Income tax 818,526; Profit after tax 1,588,902. Ties: 4,210,998 less 1,803,570 equals 2,407,428, and 2,407,428 less 818,526 equals 1,588,902. Source: https://doclib.ngxgroup.com/Financial_NewsDocs/47488_AFRICA_PRUDENTIAL_PLC-_QUARTER_2_-_FINANCIAL_STATEMENT_FOR_2026_FINANCIAL_STATEMENTS_JULY_2026.pdf CRON 20261107: H1 2026 rows completed from the issuer interim statement read in the NGX filing library copy on disk. AFRIPRUD: Cost of sales 71,573 and Gross Profit 670,745 thousands printed on page 4 of the interim statement for the six months to 30 June 2026 (Revenue 742,318 less cost of sales 71,573 equals 670,745). Operating Expenses was stored at -1,803,570,000 with a wrong sign: the statement prints personnel 968,451 plus other operating expenses 753,400 plus depreciation 33,610 plus amortisation 27,490 plus credit loss 20,619, which sums to 1,803,570 thousands and reconciles to the printed profit before finance costs and tax of 2,407,428. | CRON 20261117: 9M 2026 (nine months ended 30 September 2026) added from Africa Prudential Plc statement of profit or loss page 4, nine month 2026 column, printed in thousands of naira and stored x1,000. Printed at that column: revenue from contracts with customers 1,074,605; cost of sales -133,445; gross profit 941,160; interest income 5,846,146 and other income 124,673, which with gross profit give the printed net operating income of 6,911,979; credit loss expense 30,632 plus personnel 1,388,636 plus other operating 1,332,666 plus depreciation 46,297 plus amortisation 40,788 (operating expenses 2,839,019); profit before finance costs and tax 4,072,960, stored as Operating Profit (EBIT) and as Profit Before Tax because the filing prints no finance cost at that column; income tax expense 1,384,806; profit after tax 2,688,154; basic and diluted earnings per share 67 kobo, stored as 0.67 naira to match the EPS unit already in this file. Net profit exceeds contract revenue because this issuer earns most of its income as interest on client funds, printed separately as interest income, so the guard against a profit above revenue does not apply to this business model. Ties exactly: revenue less cost of sales equals gross profit; gross profit plus interest income plus other income less operating expenses equals the printed profit before finance costs and tax; profit before tax less income tax equals profit after tax. | CRON 20261120: Net Finance Costs added as nil for FY2025 and FY2024 from the audited statement of profit or loss, page 36 of the FY2025 annual report (_ngx_pdf/AFRIPRUD.pdf). The statement prints Profit before finance costs and tax of 4,258,110 (2025) and 2,810,359 (2024) immediately followed by Profit before income tax expense of 4,258,110 and 2,810,359, so no finance cost was charged in either year; the figure is nil, not blank. Earlier years left empty because no filed statement for them was read. Thousands of naira as printed, stored as absolute naira.

rows.label: Income Tax
rows.sign_normalized: negated to the dataset convention: stored negative, which broke the printed identity Profit Before Tax - Income Tax = Net Profit, and the column ties with it positive

rows.label: Operating Expenses
rows.note: five year financial summary, statement of profit or loss, AFRIPRUD annual report FY2025, total operating expenses printed as (3,215,773)/(2,695,177)/(2,547,307)/(1,998,868)/(1,611,912) in NGN thousand. Replaces a different expense line. Revenue less this figure reproduces the printed profit before tax for all five years.

rows.label: EPS

unitGuard.reason: unit guard: the EPS row for 9M 2026 read 670 against 0.672038 for that period's net profit divided by the shares on file, a factor of 997, which is the 1000x multiple of a per-share figure printed in a sub-unit (kobo / cents / a thousandth). Normalised to 0.67, the unit the price is quoted in.

rows.unitGuardBasis: factor = stored EPS / (the same period's net profit / shares on file); a factor within 15% of a power of ten (or its reciprocal) whose corrected value lands within 2.0x of the triangle is a UNIT error and is normalised; a stored cell of the opposite sign to the period's net profit whose magnitude is beyond 5.0x is WITHHELD with both figures named; every other cell is left exactly as filed

rows.label: Operating Margin (%)
rows.derivedCellFormula: Operating Margin (%) = Operating Profit (EBIT) / Revenue x 100

rows.label: Gross Margin (%)
rows.derivedCellFormula: Gross Margin (%) = Gross Profit / Revenue x 100

derivation.ratiosNote: ratio cells tagged derived are arithmetic on the filed figures of this security, not printed in the source

This statement is stored in NGN '000 (the filing's printed unit), not absolute units, so the value renders 1000x too small under the platform's absolute convention. The audit rule requires the cell to equal the discovery record's profit_after_tax with the unit applied (absolute 1588902000); per fix-only-by-withholding it was nulled rather than rescaled. NOTE: the whole statement (revenue and every other row of this file) is stored in NGN '000 and needs block normalisation.
